item: A rollup build that ends in an error keeps a failure hold released like the duckdb-limit hold, so the next request does not start the same build again (R172)
summary: Measured before: a RuntimeError forced in the build, 5 requests, 5 builds, no hold, boot row unknown. Now the failure keeps a hold in THIS process only (reason build-failed, stage or stage_why, exception class, consecutive failures; never the exception text), released by a larger limit, offload allowed, a 5% smaller corpus or another version; a restart retries once and the kept record carries only the run of failures across it, so a transient error never keeps the accelerator off. A build that serves, or ends in a stop of another kind, ends the run. The record's stage is the LAST REPORTED stage, not the raising statement (the key is the one the duckdb-limit hold uses). status() gains last_outcome, consecutive_failures and last_failure_class ONLY while the run is above 0: absent means 0 since the last serve. The boot step row names the class. Plain OOM stays the duckdb-limit stop; the dormant persisted path is not touched. Net bytes: the constant refresh 'change-gated' left status(); worst-case columnar.json rollup_serve row 1,553 B base -> 1,528 B (duckdb-limit hold) and 1,045 B (failure hold), pinned by a test.
